fatal_errors: The proposed Nb-based interlayer is absent from the target system and has no cited supporting evidence.
The target intervention is modulation of Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer period to 16 nm, producing semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces, not addition of a chemically distinct interlayer.
The hypothesis assumes high-temperature creep, whereas the reported transition was measured by room-temperature nanoindentation creep.

The predicted transition direction is inconsistent with the target: the semicoherent 16 nm multilayer transitions toward diffusion/interface-slip-mediated creep, not from diffusion creep toward dislocation-mediated creep.

The proposed mechanism of coherent Nb interfaces with intermediate diffusivity does not match the reported role of semicoherent interfaces, misfit dislocations, dislocation pileup, and proposed stress-induced interfacial amorphization.
explanation: The response recognizes that interface structure can mediate a transition between diffusion- and dislocation-controlled creep, but it reconstructs neither the material nor the experiment. The relevant material is the approximately 1 μm FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni HEA multilayer with a 16 nm modulation period (M16), whose semicoherent interfaces yield the minimum stress exponent and greatest reported creep resistance under room-temperature nanoindentation. The Nb-based interlayer, high-temperature conditions, baseline, mechanism, and predicted transition direction are speculative and unsupported. The proposed falsification experiment is broadly testable, but it evaluates a new hypothesis rather than discriminating the mechanism reported in the target study.
